BLOCKER: Design metadata incomplete per AGENTS/standards: affected_components, risks, out_of_scope are "Not specified" and rollback is only "Revert the change" — insufficient for a gating pipeline change before Gate 1.5.

Language rule not decided: `core/gate_predicates.py` is shipped (non-tooling) logic but affected_files contain only Python; the design must state why this is tooling/allowed-edit vs new shipped Go logic (guardrail 7).

Human-only decision is enforced by a self-asserted `--hil-confirmed` flag with no binding to an authenticated human identity; any CI/script can set it. Design must bind the flag to a verifiable non-CI principal (guardrail 3).
MAJOR: Fail-open/fail-closed semantics for Gate 0/1/2.5 are undefined: if the check tooling, config, or state store is unavailable, precheck must be explicitly fail-closed (or documented fail-open with alerting); no availability/on-startup defence is described (guardrail 2).

`--rereview` bypass is not constrained to post-change state; AC requires "re-review only after code changes" — the design must define the immutable-sha/hash invariant and refuse `--rereview` when sha is unchanged (guardrail 5, Gate 2.5 convergence).
CI-refusal for `gate_decide` is not specified (env detection, exit codes, which CI signals), so the "refuses in CI" AC is unverifiable.
`accepted_risks.until` has no expiry enforcement path (what re-check fails when `until` lapses?), leaving a permanent silent risk acceptance.

Observability gap: `gate0_check`/`gate-brief` only "print" to stdout; no structured exit codes, decision/audit log events, or metrics are specified, so gate failures are not diagnosable at scale (guardrail 10).

Ownership/reuse (CL-001): predicates may be duplicated between `core/gate_predicates.py` and `scripts/dev/*`; the design must name a single writer/owner for gate-state and the schema of the decision record (reversibility/rollback depends on it).
MINOR: Reversibility: reverting the code does not revert decision/review records already written under the new schema; a documented backfill/ignore path for orphaned records is missing (guardrails 1/6).
SCOPE follow-up items are referenced but not required to exist/be open; dangling or closed follow-ups would silently void the scope guard (referential integrity).
No tenant/RLS scoping, redaction, or retention statement for stored decisions and review evidence (guardrail 9).
Gate ordering invariant (0 → 1 → 2 → 2.5) and sha immutability are not stated as tested invariants (guardrail 5).
Recurring untested paths (`_render_review`/`_item_dispositions` index alignment, missing-item, unknown-status) remain uncovered by the listed tests.
NIT: "out_of_scope: Not specified" should enumerate explicit exclusions (e.g., no changes to Go runtime, no schema migrations) to make scope creep detectable.
Probe/key uniqueness using wall-clock nanos (recurring) — negligible but easy to make deterministic.
Config change in `config/ci-cd-gates.json` deserves a version/schema marker to avoid silent incompatibility on rollback.
SUMMARY: Verdict: not ready for Gate 1.5 — the design asserts enforcement but leaves the key guarantees (human identity binding, CI refusal, fail-closed semantics, sha immutability, observability) unspecified.
Top risks: spoofable `--hil-confirmed` defeats the human-only invariant; unspecified failure mode risks fail-open gating; incomplete design metadata and language-rule disposition block compliance.
Reusable structure (single predicates module, existing gate-brief) is directionally right; add invariant tests and decision-record ownership before proceeding.
